absent: Complete struct layouts and sizes for pressure groups, triggers, runqueues and tasks beyond the fields observed here.
Behavior of percpu collection, trigger initialization and update, work scheduling, average computation and window reset helpers not routed to this lane.
Behavior of clock sources, runqueue lock primitives, task change and group change accounting, and write section begin and end.
Meanings and numeric values of pressure states, resources, task flags, update counts, window limits and time conversion constants.
Thread, timer, wait queue and memory allocation primitives, scheduler class changes and real-time bandwidth accounting details.
Cgroup parent lookup, pressure group lookup, kernfs notification and polling, sequence file and user copy helpers.
Handlers for real-time sysctl writes and round-robin slice writes and validation beyond table bounds.
Proc creation, directory handling and output formatting helpers and exact averaging formulas.

findings.text: Provides a helper that moves a task to first-in first-out scheduling at priority one and emits a one-time warning if the underlying scheduler update fails.
Provides paired entry and exit operations that record outermost memory stall transitions for the current task and adjust pressure bookkeeping while the local queue is held with interrupts masked.
Provides allocation and release of per-cgroup pressure state with per-processor storage and parent linkage, plus task migration between groups and re-evaluation of group state across all processors.
Provides installation, removal, readiness polling and monitor thread provisioning for threshold triggers, separating low-latency privileged handling from averaged unprivileged handling.
Provides a status formatter for a pressure group and resource that refreshes averaged state under protection before emitting short, medium and long averages with an accumulated total.
Defines a persistent monitor thread created with name psimon that lowers its own priority, then alternates between interruptible sleep and polling work until a stop request arrives.
Defines a timer handler that recovers its group from timer membership, raises a wakeup indication and wakes the monitor wait queue.

Defines file operations for input-output, memory, processor and interrupt pressure files, routing open to single-instance display, write to trigger installation, poll to event readiness and release to trigger teardown.

Defines a period timer handler for real-time bandwidth that forwards through elapsed periods, invokes the period accounting step without holding the bandwidth lock, and either deactivates or rearms based on idle outcome.
Defines a build-time program whose main records the byte displacement of the pinned-count member inside the runqueue descriptor.

Protects trigger list membership, per-state reference counts and state mask, shared minimum period, window end and next update instants, totals snapshot and monitor task publication with the group trigger mutex.
Protects collection of per-processor times for averaging, next average update instant and averaged trigger list membership with the group averages mutex.
Requires queue locking with interrupts masked across stall flag updates, cross-group task transfer and per-processor restart, using local, task-pinned or scoped per-processor acquisition.

Uses release publishing and acquire consumption for the monitor task reference and file trigger reference, a grace-period wait before freeing or stopping, and a full barrier between clearing the scheduled indication and sampling state.

Polling transitions between idle and active windows: absence of monitored changes past expiry parks the next update far ahead and stops, while monitored changes initialize and prolong the window with periodic trigger refresh and delayed rescheduling.

Trigger objects move from validation and insertion to event generation and readiness signalling, ending with list removal, shared minima and mask recomputation, and monitor shutdown when no monitored states remain.
Monitor execution cycles between sleeping on a wait queue and performing polling work, consuming the wakeup indication atomically and terminating promptly when stopping is requested.

Trigger parameters must select some or full with two numeric arguments, use a nonzero window within upper bound WINDOW_MAX_US and a nonzero threshold within the window, map to a valid state with interrupt limited to full, and restrict unprivileged windows to multiples of the two-second aggregate interval.
Stall tracking preserves nesting by saving prior stall state in caller storage and performing accounting only when entering from unstalled or leaving to unstalled.

Group migration moves the saved pressure flags out of the source group and into the destination group around the membership pointer update, ignoring transient scheduler queue state that may be incoherent across a lock drop.

Restart has no effect on disabled groups and otherwise walks every possible processor under queue protection to recompute masks and restart timing from the local clock without signalling a task transition.
Status reporting merges per-processor times and refreshes averages when due while holding the averages mutex, then emits some and full rows except that system processor full is omitted.

Sampling after clearing the scheduled indication could miss a concurrent update; the sampler issues a barrier between clear and load while the updater uses an exchanging store, ensuring a missed sample forces another wakeup.

Teardown tolerates a timer firing after the final trigger removal while the group remains alive, waits for read-side completion before freeing, cancels delayed averaging work and shuts down the timer synchronously, and stops the monitor outside the trigger mutex.

Installation rejects a second trigger on the same descriptor as busy under the sequence mutex, release warns if monitored states persist at group free, destruction wakes waiters to end polling, and absent or disabled triggers yield error poll masks.

Real-time tuning exposes controls named sched_rt_period_us and sched_rt_runtime_us defaulting to one million and sched_rr_timeslice_ms derived from the base slice, with period bounded below by one and above by integer maximum, runtime bounded below by negative one and above by period, registered under kernel. Base slice defaults to RR_TIMESLICE and maximum runtime tracks MAX_BW.

When the master enable is set, reporting appears as a pressure directory containing entries for input-output, memory, processor and optionally interrupt, each created permissive for read and write and bound to its matching operation table.

Trigger writes copy at most thirty-two bytes from user space with termination, require a nonempty input, return the input length on success, and status lines distinguish some versus full with three load averages and a microsecond total.
Build metadata captures the displacement of the pinned-count field within the runqueue descriptor for consumption outside C.

Observed group state links a parent group, per-processor storage, trigger collections with per-state counts and a combined mask, window and scheduling instants, totals and averages with update timing, and mutex, timer, wait queue and atomic flag synchronization.

Observed trigger state links a parent group and optional file context, a monitored state selector, threshold and window extents with reset origin, event count and timing with pending indication, and a selector between low-latency and averaged aggregation with its wait mechanism.
